evidence.api_compatibility: No API changes whatsoever. Only documentation files, GitHub templates, and mkdocs.yml were modified.
evidence.documentation: This PR is itself a documentation overhaul. It adds two new docs (ai-content-policy.md, spec-driven-dev.md), updates contribute.md, AGENTS.md, documentation.md, working-groups/README.md, mkdocs.yml, and GitHub templates. The author cross-references all artifacts consistently and updated the PR template to include the AI content policy reminder. The deleted large-request-memory-benchmark.md was replaced with a pointer in docs/dev/README.md. mkdocs.yml was updated to include the new pages. All changes are internally consistent.
evidence.manual_release_testing: Not applicable. This is a pure documentation/policy change with no user-visible code changes, CLI behavior changes, or GUI changes.
evidence.post_approval_commits: The first approval came from @ramkrishna2910 at 2026-09-08T17:24:03Z. After that, 12 commits were pushed: addressing reviewer feedback, removing the 30-day auto-close note, reordering template sections, refining the AI policy goals, adding the in-situ review carve-out, fixing typos, restructuring headings, and adding a networking/security row to the code owners table. The first post-approval commit at 2026-09-08T18:07:05Z was addressed and re-approved by the first wave of reviewers. The final commit (d998489, adding @Geramy to code owners) was approved by @Geramy at 2026-09-09T16:44:48Z and @abn at 2026-09-10T01:15:57Z, so the latest approvals cover all post-approval changes. No commits were added after the latest approval. All post-approval commits were within the spirit and scope of the approved PR.
evidence.review: PR #3521 received 9 substantive reviews from maintainers covering the full breadth of subject areas (CLI, GUI, networking, security, CI, packaging). The review quality was high: reviewers asked clarifying questions (e.g., @sofiageo on RFC process for UI changes), challenged framing (@superm1 on edge cases), and identified policy tensions (@kenvandine on AI review tool output). The author addressed all feedback inline. The project philosophy (design for agility, user error is a bug, human-centered discourse) is reflected throughout.
evidence.security: No security-sensitive code changes. A minor addition of the word 'sweet' as an AI-agent canary was committed but then discussed in PR comments and ultimately not included in the approved merge — @jeremyfowers acknowledged the canary's self-defeating nature and removed it via discussion. The final merged content is clean of canary instructions.
evidence.tests: This PR changes only documentation and policy files — no code, no tests, no configuration. No test changes are warranted or expected.

shout_outs.reason: Provided substantive feedback on AI code review expectations, warning about false-positives in automated reviews and driving the policy to explicitly require reviewers to filter and rewrite AI tool output in their own words.
Raised a critical tension about AI code review tools posting AI prose directly on PRs, which the author resolved with a specific carve-out exception for in-situ review agents.
